newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-PLUCKY MOUSCRON PAY HEAVY PRICE FOR SUCCESS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PLUCKY MOUSCRON PAY HEAVY PRICE FOR SUCCESS.

text.p: Belgian first division fledglings Mouscron have learned success can demand a high price.
Comfortably four points clear at the top of the standings three months ago, they are now out of the title hunt, have lost their coach and a key player while two other linchpins are on the way out.
"We are victims of our success," mourned manager Willy Verhoost.
Mouscron were still four points clear of nearest rivals Club Brugge in mid-January when morale was dealt a hammer blow by news that coach Georges Leekens had signed as national trainer.

Leekens was drafted to salvage Belgium's chances of qualifying for next year's World Cup finals, replacing Wilfried Van Moer who left in disgrace after Belgium's humiliating 3-0 home defeat by the Netherlands in January.
The pill was particularly hard to swallow for Mouscron's management who learned of Leekens' move through the media.
Leekens's offer to coach Mouscron and the national team simultaneously until the end of the season was angrily rejected.
"We might have become champions if Leekens had stayed here," Verhoost said.

Leekens has partly atoned by drafting in Mouscron midfielder Dominique Lemoine and the club's sparkling pair of strikers -- Zairean-born brothers Mbo and Emile (Lokonda) Mpenza -- to the national team.
Mouscron's Serb striker Gordan Vidovic, who won Belgian nationality last month, is next on Leekens's list but the union is awaiting the go-ahead from FIFA before calling him up.
"We weren't just lucky, we also have a good team, three, and with Vidovic four players in the national team, that's nearly half our side," Verhoost said.
For the club and town of 53,000 inhabitants, the first half of the season had been a fairytale.
Mouscron finished only third in the second division last year but edged three other teams in the playoffs for the second berth in the highest division.

The plucky team, whose stadium has a capacity of only 9,200, became the talk of the town when a subtle cocktail of luck, youth and experience carefully blended by Leekens brought them instant success.
But the rise to fame also put them in the limelight, and Lemoine was the first one to leave the club last month when he accepted a lucrative offer from Espanol Barcelona.
The Mpenza brothers have already announced publicly that they are leaving but swamped by a string of offers, mainly from Italy and France, they still have to announce the name of their new club.
Many observers predicted earlier in the season that Mouscron was bound to fall prey to its inexperience, and the club has increasingly struggled to overcome weaker opponents.
They were beaten 4-1 at home by Ekeren in their most recent game.
"Leaving aside all our problems, the strain has started to tell at the end of such a season which began in fact with the playoffs," he said.
"Of course the Leekens case, Lemoine case, other cases, they all hurt. But why shouldn't we be able to get over it?" Verhoost said.
Mouscron, formed in 1965, was aiming to become a household name in Belgian first division soccer.
"We want to be a good sub-top team which will be regularly among the first six, seven and occasionally play in Europe. We don't pretend we can compete with Anderlecht or (title holders) Club Brugge.
With three more rounds to be played, Mouscron are trailing 10 points behind Lierse and eight behind Club Brugge.
